ambient_vs_soliton_clock_stability_dicho.note: Per-decade drift figures are literature compilations/estimates, not fits; the two computed anchors are Saturn (~0.43-0.45%/decade) and Uranus (~0.012%/decade).
ambient_vs_soliton_clock_stability_dicho.ordering: Saturn (ambient, lowest S, no tilted-field fiducial) >> Neptune ~ Uranus (ambient but tilted fields anchor to interior) >> Jupiter ~ brown dwarfs ~ SIMP J0136 (soliton/saturated, ~0) — clock stability requires either the soliton branch or an interior fiducial; Saturn uniquely lacks both.

skr_equinox_reversal_falsifier.prediction: Ambient-branch coupling predicts renewed N/S SKR period-ordering reversal near the May 2025 equinox (observable by Wind/STEREO WAVES; SKR < 1.2 MHz is ground-blocked).

Saturn.assessment: R_T = 0.325 R_S sits inside the diffuse core-envelope transition region that extends out to ~0.6 R_S (Mankovich & Fuller 2021); the separate thin (>2500-3000 km) He-rain stable layer that axisymmetrizes the dynamo field sits above it (Cao et al. 2020) — two distinct stratified structures.

Jupiter.assessment: R_T = 0.405 R_J lands at the outer boundary of the Juno dilute-core region (Wahl et al. 2017; Debras & Chabrier 2019).

Earth.assessment: PREM kernel centroid sits at 1.160 R_T in the lower mantle (Step 14 nonlinear Picard solution).

Sun.assessment: Tachocline at sqrt(3) R_T = 0.715 R_sun vs measured 0.713 R_sun (existing Ch5 channel).

universal_tep_satellite_expansion_law.metric_lapse_derivation: In an ambient-branch planet (M < M_cap) with an interior saturation core boundary at R_T(M) < R_p coupled to an exterior orbit a >> R_T (an inhomogeneous two-zone geometry where differential drift between R_T and a cannot be removed by a homogeneous time redefinition d tau = A(t) dt), the cosmological lapse/mode drift |d ln(omega_mode)/dt| = |d ln|g_00|/dt| = 2 H0 = 4 g_t / c paces the non-axisymmetric resonance-locked spin-to-orbit tidal torque Gamma_mode = -d Phi_mode/d phi = dL_orb/dt = -dJ_p/dt (Fuller et al. 2016; Lainey et al. 2020), yielding da/dt / a = +(2/3)|d ln(omega_mode)/dt| = +(4/3) H0 = 8 g_t / (3 c) = (10.48 Gyr)^(-1), dL_orb/L_orb = +(2/3) H0 dt = -dJ_p/L_orb, d ln|E_orb|/dt = -(4/3) H0 (signed dE_orb/|E_orb| = +(4/3) H0 dt), and <de/dt>_sec = 0.
universal_tep_satellite_expansion_law.jupiter_soliton_branch_positive_control: Jupiter (M = 317.8 M_earth > M_cap = 194.2 M_earth) sits on the rigid soliton branch rather than the drifting ambient branch; correspondingly, its Galilean moons in the 4:2:1 Laplace resonance retain high near-classical Q_Jup = (3.56 +- 0.56)e4 (Lainey et al. 2009) rather than the rapid ~10.5 Gyr ambient-branch expansion observed at Earth (Q ~ 12) and Saturn (Q_Titan = 124 +- 22).

titan_angular_momentum_budget_audit.assessment: Even under resonance-locked Q_eff = 124 +- 22 (Lainey et al. 2020), Titan transfers < ~0.6% of Saturn's spin angular momentum over Solar-System age — and its fractional orbital expansion rate da/dt / a = (10.81 +- 1.91 Gyr)^(-1) matches both Earth's Moon (10.06 Gyr) and the zero-parameter TEP cosmological drift law da/dt / a = (4/3) H0 = 8 g_t / (3 c) = (10.48 Gyr)^(-1), which simultaneously reproduces the 50x apparent-Q variation across all six measured Saturnian moons.

bryan_2020_pmo_breakup_envelope_test.falsifier: Any unbraked planetary-mass companion or brown dwarf with M > M_cap = 0.61 M_Jup exceeding v_cap / v_breakup = (eta_0 / k_MOI) sqrt(min(1, S)) (0.478 at SIMP J0136 S=0.76, and 0.630 at S>=1) falsifies the soliton angular-momentum capacity bound.

terrestrial_moi_pressure_vs_iron_core_sp.mercury_iron_core_note: Mercury (P_c = 24.5 GPa, rho = 5.427 g/cm^3) and Mars (P_c = 24.9 GPa, rho = 3.934 g/cm^3) share similar central pressures; Venus (141 GPa) and Earth (173 GPa) satisfy the strict P_c > K_0 (~100 GPa) silicate self-compression threshold independently (2k_MOI/S = 1.024 +- 0.008, rho_T = 18.6 +- 0.5 g/cm^3), whereas Mercury's low k_MOI = 0.346 reflects its ~70-85% iron core mass fraction (rho > 5.2 g/cm^3).
